known_information: The original Keyboard Manager case maps the Copilot chord to an application/context-menu key; after using it, NVDA+t stops responding until NVDA restarts.
The author tried the requested0.99update and explicitly said it did not resolve the issue.

The new0.102.3001participant describes a different Quick Accent case: the picker opens, selected characters are not announced and insertion fails while NVDA is active; disabling/suspending NVDA changes the result.

Current Quick Accent source separates its native low-level keyboard listener from managed SendInput-based insertion. It can therefore display a picker without proving successful insertion or accessibility announcements.
issue_context.analysis: Keep the two module-specific paths separate instead of treating a guessed Windows hook priority as a proven cause. This is accessibility interoperability work, not an instruction to stop using a screen reader or run permanently elevated. The text is sufficient for controlled maintainer reproduction.
issue_context.summary: The thread now contains two NVDA interoperability regressions in different modules; the earlier update request was answered and must not be repeated.
initial_investigation: Read all replies, including the answered update request and the new different-module scenario. Inspected current Quick Accent keyboard listener and SendInput producer locations.
Did not accept an external AI hook-priority explanation as evidence; no NVDA runtime, hardware Copilot-key or screen-reader test was executed.
inferences: Picker visibility proves activation only, not character injection or screen-reader announcement. The Copilot/NVDA shortcut failure need not share the Quick Accent cause.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unverified hypotheses: Keyboard Manager synthetic modifier state may disrupt later NVDA shortcuts, while Quick Accent may separately fail insertion or announcement. A shared hook-priority explanation is not proven.

confidence.rationale: Detailed contrasting reproductions support investigation, but the two mechanisms and exact failing input/announcement producers remain unmeasured.

plan: Run the two reported sequences independently, recording input routing and resulting NVDA shortcut/announcement behavior.
For Keyboard Manager compare the Copilot chord remap with direct context-menu input and inspect modifier down/up state.
For Quick Accent distinguish successful selection, successful SendInput delivery and UIA announcement; correct only the demonstrated boundary and preserve assistive-technology operation.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate NVDA input and announcement interoperability by module
verification: NVDA+t works before and after the remapped context-menu action without restarting NVDA.
Quick Accent inserts the selected character with NVDA running and exposes a meaningful selection announcement.
Other mappings and ordinary typing retain balanced modifier events; no elevated-process requirement or global screen-reader bypass is introduced.

steps: Confirm NVDA+t reads the title, invoke the Copilot-to-context-menu remap, then retry NVDA+t without restarting either program.
In a separate Quick Accent test, hold R, activate the picker, change selection and release R; record insertion and announcement independently.
Use module on/off and direct-input controls to identify the failing event/announcement boundary; do not infer hook priority from picker visibility.
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.102.3001and current development build, with recorded NVDA version
reproduce.expected_result: The original shortcut remains usable after remapping; the selected accent is inserted and accessible without restarting or suspending NVDA.
prerequisites: Windows test desktop with NVDA running, a Copilot-key-capable keyboard for the original case, and the reported Polish/other layout recorded.
Use a test-owned text document; preserve screen-reader accessibility and existing mappings.

fix_assessment.rationale: Both reports provide discriminating sequences and a screen-reader contrast, but no exact swallowed/synthetic event or announcement defect has been established.

judgment.rationale: Keep the two module-specific paths separate instead of treating a guessed Windows hook priority as a proven cause. This is accessibility interoperability work, not an instruction to stop using a screen reader or run permanently elevated. The text is sufficient for controlled maintainer reproduction.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the original Keyboard Manager/NVDA shortcut sequence and the separate Quick Accent insertion/announcement sequence with NVDA active throughout the supported test.
